After whatsoever there is an affix enjoined, wether verbal or crude-form, that which begins therewith in the form in which it appears when the affix follows it, is called an अङ्ग 'Inflective base'.

Terms: गुरु

The word अनु 'alongside of' is optionally compounded with the word indicative of that whose length the particle expresses and compound so formed is called अव्ययीभाव।

Terms: समास-अव्ययीभाव
Where a word is governed by a कर्मप्रवचनीयाः
in the sense of 'more than' उपोऽधिके च

there the 7th case-affix (locative) is used.

Terms: विभक्ति-7

By the action (भाव) of whatsoever, the time of another action is indicated, that takes the 7th case-affix.

Terms: विभक्ति-7

After the word यस्क etc. there is the लुक् elision of the गोत्र affix when the word of itself and not as part of a compound epithet dependent on another word, takes the plural; but not in the feminine.

Terms: गोत्र-elision

The affix श्यन् is optionally used after the verb यस् 'to strive' when it is used without a preposition and when a सार्वधातुक affix denoting an agent, follows. 

Terms: श्यन्

The affix वरच् in the sense of 'agent having such a habit etc.' comes after the verb या when it ends with the affix यङ्।

Terms: वरच्

When the परस्मैपद affixes of the Potential follow, then यासुट् acutely accented, is their augment and the termination is regarded as having an indicatory ङ्।

Terms: यासुट्

When a consonant precedes the final य in a verbal अङ्ग (stem) this य is also elided before an आर्धधातुक affix.

Terms: आर्धधातुक changes

The final अ and इ (both long and short) of a भ अङ्ग (stem) are elided before a तद्धित affix.

Terms: अ & इ elision

The participial affixes do not take the इट् augment after those roots, to which another suffix can optionally be added, with or without this augment इ।

Terms: इट् augment
